beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: Nobody hears a recording
beats.body: The tab is captured as a picture only, and the voice plays through a muted element. Its stream is mixed into the file through Web Audio instead, on a track that is there from the first frame, because the file cannot take a track that arrives after it started.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the browser has stopped and the sound is converted. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.

Only the voice's own lines of the transcript are kept. At the end the audio is cut to the origin and the end, so it is exact to the sample against the stamps. The worklet writes silence while nothing plays.

nodes.name: Replay page

nodes.name: Video encoder

nodes.name: Nix

nodes.name: Frame order

nodes.description: A page may put a frame at most two rounds of seconds ahead of the encoder and waits for room otherwise, which bounds how many frames are held.

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Runs a recording's two passes: proves ffmpeg first, records the talk in a live page, keeps it, then has it drawn frame by frame
nodes.description: Pass 1's browser is started with audio allowed to play and a fake microphone playing a second of silence, because voice will not start without a microphone and would hear Chromium's default tone as somebody speaking. It captures nothing and needs no GPU: nobody looks at the page, whose reports are what the server hands the voice. A board drawn at another version while it was recorded fails the recording and nothing is kept, since no one picture goes with that talk. The talk is written before pass 2 starts, so a render that fails keeps it. Both passes find ffmpeg and start their browser through the same two helpers (lib/tools.ts). An interrupt stops the browser at once, so every call waiting on it fails and nothing is written. The recording page names the repository of the command's vault as repoA, so it reads that vault.

nodes.name: Page driver
nodes.responsibility: Waits until the page is ready, starts it from a user gesture, follows each step, then streams the voice out and reads the talk's events
nodes.description: Everything the page says crosses as the shared recording state or the talk's log and is parsed as such, so a page from another build is refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.name: ffmpeg
nodes.responsibility: Encodes the frames and the voice into one file: H.264 and AAC in MP4, or VP9 and Opus in WebM, the index at the front
nodes.description: Named by ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, found on PATH, or run through Nix. A recording needs it: without one, the recording is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Recording page
nodes.responsibility: The server's own page on one board: shows the pane alone, paces each step by the voice, and records the talk, never the picture
nodes.description: The voice plays through a muted audio element, so nobody hears a recording, and talk capture taps the same stream. The page hands over the voice as a 16-bit mono 48 kHz WAV and the talk's events by value. It captures no picture: the replay page draws every frame again from the talk.

nodes.name: Replay command
nodes.responsibility: Renders a kept talk to a video again, in either theme, with no voice and no board
nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only to serve the page. A talk that cannot be read, or one of another format version, is refused as a usage error before a browser starts. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones record uses (recording-output.ts).

nodes.name: Frame renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws a talk frame by frame on several replay pages at once, each in its own Chromium: every page steps through every frame, and each captures its own seconds for the encoder
nodes.description: One frame is 1/30 s of talk, exactly 1600 samples of the voice, so frame n and sample 1600n are the same moment. Chromium draws in software (--disable-gpu) and without partial raster, so two renders of a talk are identical, and without the frame-rate limit, so a screenshot does not wait for the display. A screenshot costs several times what drawing a frame does, so the talk is drawn by up to six pages at once, a quarter of the machine's threads and one for every 300 frames: page k captures seconds k, k + n and so on, and draws the frames between without capturing them, since a frame depends on the ones before it. A frame is the same whichever page draws it. Before the first frame each page proves it counts the talk's frames and its window is 1920x1080. A frame is taken as JPEG at quality 92, since the picture is encoded again as 4:2:0 anyway. Handed no ffmpeg, as semantic replay hands none, it finds and proves one first. The file moves into place only once the browsers have stopped and ffmpeg has exited. A render that fails on any page stops the others, keeps the talk and names the replay command that renders it again.

nodes.name: Talk files
nodes.responsibility: Says where a talk is kept, writes it as talk.json and voice.wav in one atomic rename, and reads one back through the talk's schema
nodes.description: Every recording keeps its talk under the state directory's recordings, where the newest 10 stay. --talk keeps it in a new directory of its own that is never pruned. A place that already exists is refused before anything starts. A talk read back must parse as a talk and its voice.wav must hold as many samples as talk.json says, or it is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Talk capture
nodes.responsibility: Taps the voice through an AudioWorklet and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own 48 kHz clock
nodes.description: The origin is the moment the voice goes live, where the video begins. A stamp is late by at most one audio buffer, about 10 to 21 ms on Linux, which is under one frame. Only the voice's own lines of the transcript are kept. At the end the audio is cut to the origin and the end, so it is exact to the sample against the stamps. The worklet writes silence while nothing plays.

nodes.name: Replay page
nodes.responsibility: The server's page asked for with ?replay=1: draws a talk's board from the talk alone, one frame at a time on a stepped clock
nodes.description: It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. Loading a talk plays the board's entrance through first, uncaptured, so frame 0 shows the board at rest. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time, a picture's traffic at where its picture's clock stands. An animation on another timeline, or a read of another board, fails the render and names the frame.

nodes.name: Video encoder
nodes.responsibility: Finds ffmpeg, proves it has the encoders the file needs, and turns the JPEG frames and the voice into that file
nodes.description: ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG comes first, and one named there that does not run is refused by that name, never passed over. Then ffmpeg on PATH, then nix run nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless. With none of them, ENCODER_UNAVAILABLE names both ways to get one. MP4 needs libx264 and aac, and WebM needs libvpx-vp9 and libopus. The frames are converted from full-range BT.601 to BT.709 limited range and tagged so, and the voice is padded to the last frame.

nodes.name: Nix
nodes.responsibility: Runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless from the machine's registry when no ffmpeg is found
nodes.description: nix run starts the package's own program in its place, so the frame pipe and signals reach ffmpeg itself. The first run fetches the package, which can take minutes.

nodes.name: Frame order
nodes.responsibility: Hands the pages' frames to the one ffmpeg in order, holding a frame that arrives before its turn
nodes.description: A page may put a frame at most two rounds of seconds ahead of the encoder and waits for room otherwise, which bounds how many frames are held.

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.

nodes.responsibility: Renders a kept talk to a video again, in either theme, with no voice and no board

nodes.name: Frame renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws a talk frame by frame on several replay pages at once, each in its own Chromium: every page steps through every frame, and each captures its own seconds for the encoder
nodes.description: One frame is 1/30 s of talk, exactly 1600 samples of the voice, so frame n and sample 1600n are the same moment. Chromium draws in software (--disable-gpu) and without partial raster, so two renders of a talk are identical, and without the frame-rate limit, so a screenshot does not wait for the display. A screenshot costs several times what drawing a frame does, so the talk is drawn by up to six pages at once, a quarter of the machine's threads and one for every 300 frames: page k captures seconds k, k + n and so on, and draws the frames between without capturing them, since a frame depends on the ones before it. A frame is the same whichever page draws it. Before the first frame each page proves it counts the talk's frames and its window is 1920x1080. A frame is taken as JPEG at quality 92, since the picture is encoded again as 4:2:0 anyway. Handed no ffmpeg, as semantic replay hands none, it finds and proves one first. The file moves into place only once the browsers have stopped and ffmpeg has exited. A render that fails on any page stops the others, keeps the talk and names the replay command that renders it again.

nodes.name: Talk files
nodes.responsibility: Says where a talk is kept, writes it as talk.json and voice.wav in one atomic rename, and reads one back through the talk's schema
nodes.description: Every recording keeps its talk under the state directory's recordings, where the newest 10 stay. --talk keeps it in a new directory of its own that is never pruned. A place that already exists is refused before anything starts. A talk read back must parse as a talk and its voice.wav must hold as many samples as talk.json says, or it is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Talk capture
nodes.responsibility: Taps the voice through an AudioWorklet and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own 48 kHz clock
nodes.description: The origin is the moment the voice goes live, where the video begins. A stamp is late by at most one audio buffer, about 10 to 21 ms on Linux, which is under one frame. Only the voice's own lines of the transcript are kept. At the end the audio is cut to the origin and the end, so it is exact to the sample against the stamps. The worklet writes silence while nothing plays.

nodes.name: Replay page
nodes.responsibility: The server's page asked for with ?replay=1: draws a talk's board from the talk alone, one frame at a time on a stepped clock
nodes.description: It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time, a picture's traffic at where its picture's clock stands. nodes.name: Video encoder

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Runs a recording's two passes: proves ffmpeg first, records the talk in a live page, keeps it, then has it drawn frame by frame
nodes.description: Pass 1's browser is started with audio allowed to play and a fake microphone playing a second of silence, because voice will not start without a microphone and would hear Chromium's default tone as somebody speaking. It captures nothing and needs no GPU: nobody looks at the page, whose reports are what the server hands the voice. A board drawn at another version while it was recorded fails the recording and nothing is kept, since no one picture goes with that talk. The talk is written before pass 2 starts, so a render that fails keeps it. Both passes find ffmpeg and start their browser through the same two helpers (lib/tools.ts). An interrupt stops the browser at once, so every call waiting on it fails and nothing is written. The recording page names the repository of the command's vault as repoA, so it reads that vault.

nodes.name: Page driver

nodes.description: Everything the page says crosses as the shared recording state or the talk's log and is parsed as such, so a page from another build is refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.name: ffmpeg
nodes.responsibility: Encodes the frames and the voice into one file: H.264 and AAC in MP4, or VP9 and Opus in WebM, the index at the front
nodes.description: Named by ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, found on PATH, or run through Nix. A recording needs it: without one, the recording is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Recording page
nodes.responsibility: The server's own page on one board: shows the pane alone, paces each step by the voice, and records the talk, never the picture
nodes.description: The voice plays through a muted audio element, so nobody hears a recording, and talk capture taps the same stream. The page hands over the voice as a 16-bit mono 48 kHz WAV and the talk's events by value. It captures no picture: the replay page draws every frame again from the talk.

nodes.name: Replay command
nodes.responsibility: Renders a kept talk to a video again, in either theme, with no voice and no board

nodes.name: Frame renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws a talk frame by frame on several replay pages at once, each in its own Chromium: every page steps through every frame, and each captures its own seconds for the encoder
nodes.description: One frame is 1/30 s of talk, exactly 1600 samples of the voice, so frame n and sample 1600n are the same moment. Chromium draws in software (--disable-gpu) and without partial raster, so two renders of a talk are identical, and without the frame-rate limit, so a screenshot does not wait for the display. A screenshot costs several times what drawing a frame does, so the talk is drawn by up to six pages at once, a quarter of the machine's threads and one for every 300 frames: page k captures seconds k, k + n and so on, and draws the frames between without capturing them, since a frame depends on the ones before it. A frame is the same whichever page draws it. Before the first frame each page proves it counts the talk's frames and its window is 1920x1080. A frame is taken as JPEG at quality 92, since the picture is encoded again as 4:2:0 anyway. Handed no ffmpeg, as semantic replay hands none, it finds and proves one first. The file moves into place only once the browsers have stopped and ffmpeg has exited. A render that fails on any page stops the others, keeps the talk and names the replay command that renders it again.

nodes.name: Talk files
nodes.responsibility: Says where a talk is kept, writes it as talk.json and voice.wav in one atomic rename, and reads one back through the talk's schema
nodes.description: Every recording keeps its talk under the state directory's recordings, where the newest 10 stay. --talk keeps it in a new directory of its own that is never pruned. A place that already exists is refused before anything starts. A talk read back must parse as a talk and its voice.wav must hold as many samples as talk.json says, or it is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Talk capture
nodes.responsibility: Taps the voice through an AudioWorklet and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own 48 kHz clock
nodes.description: The origin is the moment the voice goes live, where the video begins. A stamp is late by at most one audio buffer, about 10 to 21 ms on Linux, which is under one frame. Only the voice's own lines of the transcript are kept. At the end the audio is cut to the origin and the end, so it is exact to the sample against the stamps. The worklet writes silence while nothing plays.

nodes.name: Replay page
nodes.responsibility: The server's page asked for with ?replay=1: draws a talk's board from the talk alone, one frame at a time on a stepped clock
nodes.description: It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. Loading a talk plays the board's entrance through first, uncaptured, so frame 0 shows the board at rest. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time, a picture's traffic at where its picture's clock stands. An animation on another timeline, or a read of another board, fails the render and names the frame.

nodes.name: Video encoder
nodes.responsibility: Finds ffmpeg, proves it has the encoders the file needs, and turns the JPEG frames and the voice into that file
nodes.description: ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG comes first, and one named there that does not run is refused by that name, never passed over. Then ffmpeg on PATH, then nix run nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless. With none of them, ENCODER_UNAVAILABLE names both ways to get one. MP4 needs libx264 and aac, and WebM needs libvpx-vp9 and libopus. The frames are converted from full-range BT.601 to BT.709 limited range and tagged so, and the voice is padded to the last frame.

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.

nodes.description: Every recording keeps its talk under the state directory's recordings, where the newest 10 stay. --talk keeps it in a new directory of its own that is never pruned. A place that already exists is refused before anything starts. A talk read back must parse as a talk and its voice.wav must hold as many samples as talk.json says, or it is refused before a browser starts.

nodes.name: Talk capture
nodes.responsibility: Taps the voice through an AudioWorklet and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own 48 kHz clock
nodes.description: The origin is the moment the voice goes live, where the video begins. A stamp is late by at most one audio buffer, about 10 to 21 ms on Linux, which is under one frame. Only the voice's own lines of the transcript are kept. At the end the audio is cut to the origin and the end, so it is exact to the sample against the stamps. The worklet writes silence while nothing plays.

nodes.name: Replay page
nodes.responsibility: The server's page asked for with ?replay=1: draws a talk's board from the talk alone, one frame at a time on a stepped clock
nodes.description: It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. Loading a talk plays the board's entrance through first, uncaptured, so frame 0 shows the board at rest. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time, a picture's traffic at where its picture's clock stands. An animation on another timeline, or a read of another board, fails the render and names the frame.

nodes.name: Video encoder
nodes.responsibility: Finds ffmpeg, proves it has the encoders the file needs, and turns the JPEG frames and the voice into that file
nodes.description: ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG comes first, and one named there that does not run is refused by that name, never passed over. Then ffmpeg on PATH, then nix run nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless. nodes.name: Nix

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.

walkthroughs.name: Why a picture is refused rather than approximated

beats.heading: A browser only while there is work
beats.body: No Chromium is started until a job arrives, and it is stopped with the rasterizer. The process lives in its own group with its own temp root so the whole of it can be reaped, whatever it spawned.

beats.heading: The page says it is ready, in so many words
beats.body: Before anything is photographed the page is asked whether the diagram faces are loaded, the animation is paused at its first frame, and the SVG is the size the job named. A picture taken before that would differ run to run.

beats.heading: The wrong size is a refusal, not a crop
beats.body: The answered bitmap is measured from its own header against the size the bounds asked for. Cropping or scaling it here would hand back a picture that quietly is not what was asked for.

walkthroughs.name: How a walkthrough becomes a video

beats.heading: Two passes: first the talk, then the picture
beats.body: A recording is made in two passes. The first lets the voice pace the walkthrough on a live page and keeps only the talk: the voice's sound, and when each step and subtitle line came. The second draws the picture again from that talk, frame by frame, with no voice and no capture.

beats.heading: The page paces the talk
beats.body: Where a walkthrough stands is the browser's, and only the page hears when the voice has finished a step, so the page moves itself on. The recorder outside only starts it and follows what it says.

beats.heading: One clock stamps the voice and every step
beats.body: The voice plays through a muted element, so nobody hears a recording. Talk capture taps the same stream through Web Audio and stamps each step, subtitle line and drawn version on the audio's own clock. The talk is written as talk.json and voice.wav before any picture is drawn, so a failed render keeps it.

beats.heading: Every frame is drawn before it is captured
beats.body: The replay page reads the board only from the talk. Its glides, fades, subtitles and traffic run on a clock the renderer steps 1/30 s at a time, and even a frame a library asks of the browser runs on that clock. A frame is captured only once it is drawn and still, so no frame is held or dropped, with or without a GPU and under any load. An animation on a timeline the clock cannot stand fails the render.

beats.heading: ffmpeg makes the file, or nothing starts
beats.body: The frames go to ffmpeg as JPEG, with voice.wav beside them, and ffmpeg writes H.264 and AAC, or VP9 and Opus. The recorder takes ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG, then ffmpeg on PATH, then runs nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless through Nix. With none of them it refuses before any browser starts, and says how to get one.

beats.heading: A whole file, or nothing
beats.body: The file moves into place only once the render's browser has stopped and ffmpeg has exited. An interrupt anywhere before that stops the browser at once and leaves nothing where the file goes.

beats.heading: A kept talk renders again
beats.body: The render needs only the talk, so semantic replay renders a kept talk to a new file: in the other theme, or after a renderer fix. It needs the Archboard server to serve the page, and no board, no Codex and no voice. A render that fails keeps the talk and names this command.

beats.heading: One browser module, two uses
beats.body: Pictures and recordings start Chromium through the same module: the rasterizer once, a recording twice, once for the talk and once for its frames. Each browser has its own process group and temporary root, and each stop proves the group and the root are gone.
